macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Wall Street futures rebound as oil retreats amid renewed U.S.-Iran tensions
items.summary: U.S. stock index futures edged higher as oil prices and global markets steadied after fresh U.S. strikes on Iran reignited geopolitical anxiety. Reuters also reported that leverage in U.S. equity funding markets remains stretched, reflecting elevated demand for stock-market borrowing.

items.title: China’s producer prices surge for a fourth straight month
items.summary: China’s producer price inflation rose for a fourth consecutive month in June to its highest level since July 2022, while consumer prices also increased. The data point to persistent cost pressures for domestic manufacturers.

items.title: Fed's John Williams says he does not expect a sustained energy-price spike
items.summary: New York Fed President John Williams said he is not expecting the recent geopolitical flare-up to cause a sustained rise in energy prices over the rest of the year. The comments are relevant for rate expectations and inflation monitoring.

items.title: U.S. labor market remains in a slow-hire, slow-fire mode
items.summary: Reuters reported that weekly U.S. jobless claims fell, supporting views that the labor market remains resilient despite a sharp slowdown in job growth in June. The same feed noted that existing home sales unexpectedly fell as high prices and elevated mortgage rates discouraged buyers.

items.title: Global market snapshot: stocks mixed as tech and Europe move unevenly
items.summary: MarketScreener’s 24-hour topic feed showed Samsung Electronics as the most mentioned mover, while the DAX was little changed and the Nasdaq 100 was among the weaker major U.S. benchmarks in the broader recent move set. The feed also highlighted strength in select European stocks such as Zalando and LSEG.

items.title: Germany’s business sentiment improves, but recovery seen taking time
items.summary: Ifo said German business sentiment rose in June, but also warned that Germany’s economic recovery will take time. Reuters-linked MarketScreener coverage also noted that German industrial orders rose more than expected in May.

items.title: PBOC adviser sees room for a rate cut
items.summary: A Reuters-distributed MarketScreener item said a senior adviser to China’s central bank sees potential for a rate cut. The comment adds to expectations that Chinese policymakers may support growth if disinflation pressures persist.

items.title: Australian shares wobble as Fed caution offsets commodity optimism
items.summary: MarketScreener reported that Australian equities weakened as caution around the Fed tempered optimism tied to higher oil prices. The same regional feed showed Japan’s Topix rising while the Nikkei was pressured by tech weakness.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin holds near $64K as risk appetite improves and oil eases
items.summary: Bitcoin traded around $64,000 to $64,600 over the past day, with market commentary linking the move to lower oil prices and broader risk-on sentiment. The market also saw more than $250 million in crypto liquidations in 24 hours, mostly short positions.

items.title: U.S. Senate pushes CLARITY Act crypto market structure vote
items.summary: Crypto markets reacted to renewed Senate momentum on the CLARITY Act, a key U.S. market-structure bill. Coverage highlighted the legislation as a central regulatory catalyst for Bitcoin, Ethereum, and other major tokens.

items.title: Hong Kong SFC tightens exchange security rules
items.summary: Hong Kong’s Securities and Futures Commission ordered crypto platforms to abandon SMS authentication, signaling continued regulatory scrutiny of exchange security practices. The move adds to a broader global compliance push on custodians and trading venues.

items.title: Coinbase legal chief Paul Grewal exits before CLARITY vote
items.summary: Coinbase’s legal leadership changed just as Washington debates the CLARITY Act, making the timing notable for U.S. crypto policy. The departure comes amid ongoing scrutiny of exchange regulation and market structure.

items.title: Bitdeer opens $36 million Nevada factory to expand Bitcoin mining
items.summary: Bitdeer announced a new $36 million Nevada facility, a significant infrastructure development in Bitcoin mining. The move underscores continued capital investment in U.S.-based mining capacity.

items.title: Ripple-linked banks gain attention as SWIFT tests blockchain payments
items.summary: XRP rose after reports that SWIFT is tapping Ripple-linked banks for blockchain-based payments experimentation. The development has renewed investor focus on enterprise blockchain payment rails and XRP’s role in them.

items.title: Ethereum Foundation highlights limits of AI in bug discovery
items.summary: The Ethereum Foundation published a note explaining why AI still struggles to find real software bugs reliably. The update is relevant to blockchain security and the practical limits of AI-assisted auditing.

items.title: PayPal extends PYUSD stablecoin to Polygon’s Open Money Stack
items.summary: PayPal continued expanding its PYUSD stablecoin footprint by bringing it to Polygon’s Open Money Stack. The move adds another notable enterprise-backed development in stablecoin infrastructure.

items.title: BlackRock launches tokenized money market fund on Solana and Ethereum
items.summary: BlackRock launched a tokenized money market fund across Solana and Ethereum, reinforcing momentum in tokenized real-world assets and on-chain treasury products. The product is designed to support stablecoin reserves with cash and U.S. Treasuries.

items.title: Aon tests stablecoin payments for insurance premiums
items.summary: Aon is piloting stablecoin payments for insurance premiums with Coinbase and Paxos, signaling growing corporate experimentation with blockchain-based settlement. The pilot suggests stablecoins are moving further into traditional financial workflows.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: OpenAI rolls out GPT-Live across paid and free tiers
items.summary: OpenAI has fully released GPT-Live, a full-duplex voice feature that can listen and speak simultaneously, to Go, Plus, and Pro users, with GPT-Live-1 mini serving free users. The rollout is being described as a major upgrade to ChatGPT Voice and part of OpenAI’s push into more natural real-time interaction.

items.title: OpenAI broadens ChatGPT with GPT-5.6 and ChatGPT Work
items.summary: Techmeme reports that OpenAI has broadly released GPT-5.6 and launched ChatGPT Work, an AI agent for gathering context across apps and files to create documents on Mac and Windows. The release adds a new product layer aimed at workplace automation and productivity.

items.title: Meta releases Muse Spark 1.1 for coding via public API preview
items.summary: Meta has released Muse Spark 1.1, which is described as a step change over the first generation and more capable at coding. The model is available to U.S. developers through a public API preview.

items.title: Cognition launches SWE-1.7 with high-speed inference
items.summary: Cognition has released SWE-1.7, trained from Kimi K2.7 and available in Devin at 1,000 tokens per second. The company says the model approaches frontier-level performance at a lower cost.

items.title: SpaceXAI and Cursor launch Grok 4.5 for long-running professional tasks
items.summary: SpaceXAI has launched Grok 4.5, a model built in partnership with Cursor for difficult, long-running legal, finance, and coding tasks. The release signals continued competition in specialized AI models for enterprise work.

items.title: Meta announces first 1GW data center in Canada
items.summary: Meta says it will build its first Canadian data center in Alberta, a 1GW facility expected to cost about $9 billion and take two to three years to complete. The announcement underscores the infrastructure race behind large-scale AI expansion.

items.title: Ant Group’s Lingbo Technology releases two open-source models
items.summary: PulseAugur reports that Ant Group’s Lingbo Technology has released LingBot-World 2.0 for real-time interactive world generation and LingBot-Video for embodied AI video generation. Both are open-source model releases aimed at world simulation and multimodal generation.

items.title: Anthropic releases Claude Fable 5
items.summary: PulseAugur reports that Anthropic has released Claude Fable 5, described as its latest and most advanced AI model. Separate coverage suggests the model is being positioned as a flagship release in Anthropic’s lineup.

items.title: OpenAI faces scrutiny in copyright trial over ChatGPT evidence
items.summary: TechCrunch reports that the New York Times says OpenAI hid evidence in the ChatGPT copyright trial. The development adds legal pressure around training data, copyright, and model transparency.

items.title: Gradium raises $100M seed backed by Nvidia
items.summary: TechCrunch reports that Paris-based AI voice startup Gradium has raised a $100 million seed round with backing from Nvidia. The deal reflects continued investor interest in AI voice infrastructure and foundational tooling.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Electronic Arts closes $55 billion go-private sale
items.summary: EA officially completed its $55 billion sale to Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund, Silver Lake Partners, and Affinity Partners, marking one of the biggest gaming-industry deals in years.

items.title: Epic Games settles lawsuit with former Fortnite leaker
items.summary: Epic Games reached a settlement with former contractor Hayden Cohen, ending a high-profile dispute over alleged leaks of confidential Fortnite collaboration plans.

items.title: Sony clarifies physical media plans for PS5
items.summary: Sony said production of physical game discs for new PlayStation 5 titles will end in January 2028, with future releases available digitally through the PlayStation Store and at retail.

items.title: Microsoft reportedly increases investment in MachineGames
items.summary: Insider reporting says Microsoft is significantly increasing its investment in MachineGames after the studio’s recent commercial success and the continued strength of the Wolfenstein brand.

items.title: Xbox Game Pass July 2026 lineup announced
items.summary: VGC reports that Microsoft revealed the games and updates coming to Xbox Game Pass across its July 2026 tiers.

items.title: IO confirms Project Fantasy will continue independently after Xbox split
items.summary: IO Interactive said its Project Fantasy is still moving forward independently following the Xbox split, keeping the fantasy RPG in development.

items.title: Xbox layoffs reportedly hit id Software and Obsidian
items.summary: VGC reports that Microsoft’s restructuring led to significant layoffs, including cuts to id Software’s coding team and 60–70 developers at Obsidian.

items.title: WayForward announces next Shantae game
items.summary: WayForward unveiled the next Shantae title at Anime Expo, with a release window set for 2027.

items.title: Halo: Campaign Evolved boxed edition will include physical discs
items.summary: A boxed version of Halo: Campaign Evolved will include physical discs, with the publisher emphasizing tangible collector appeal.

items.title: Pokémon announces charity Champions tournament
items.summary: The Pokémon Company is organizing a charity Pokémon Champions tournament featuring a lineup of unusual celebrity competitors, adding an esports-style event to its broader competitive scene.
